llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses 'find /home/user/testDir -type f' to enumerate all regular files and 'find /home/user/testDir -mindepth 1 -type d' for all subdirectories, matching the instruction's scope exactly.
stat -c '%a' outputs octal permission strings (e.g. '644', '755') which match the expected values in the evaluator rules.
The -mindepth 1 flag correctly excludes testDir itself from the directory permission check, so only subdirectories are evaluated.
Metric checks all file permissions equal '644' (0.5 pts) and all directory permissions equal '755' (0.5 pts), covering both sub-goals from the instruction with partial scoring.
Negative-control resistance is adequate: initial state has files at mixed permissions (755/644/777), so not all files will be 644 before the agent acts.

The if file_perms / if dir_perms guards prevent false positives from empty lists but could cause a false negative (0 score) if testDir has no files or no subdirectories; however the setup guarantees both exist.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: if the task setup could ever produce an empty testDir, consider returning partial credit (0.5) when one list is empty but the other passes, to avoid unexpected 0.0 scores.
